question.text: A Category III AIF holds a portfolio of listed equities, unlisted equities, listed debt securities, and exchange-traded index futures. For which category of investment is an independent valuer MANDATORY under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Listed equities and exchange-traded index futures
Unlisted equities only — listed debt can use market prices
Unlisted securities AND listed debt securities
All four categories, regardless of market availability

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 14.14, 'Category III AIFs shall undertake valuation of their investment in UNLISTED SECURITIES AND LISTED DEBT SECURITIES by an independent valuer'. Listed equities and exchange-traded derivatives are marked-to-market using market prices, not a valuer. **The Trap:** Option B misses listed debt. Option A is inverted. Option D over-reaches. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests this; XIX-C drills into WHY listed debt needs a valuer — many corporate bonds have thin OTC market and no daily screen price, requiring FBIL-based or matrix pricing. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For listed debt, insist your valuer uses FBIL/FIMMDA yields as primary input, not the last exchange-traded print (which may be stale by weeks). Document the hierarchy in your Valuation Policy.
